title: Insulation Rebates in Allentown 2026: PPL Up to $500
desc: PPL Electric pays Allentown homeowners up to $200 or $500 each for attic, exterior wall and rim joist insulation, plus up to $150 for air sealing. How to qualify.
lead: PPL Electric pays rebates on three kinds of insulation and on air sealing. In an older Allentown home, that is often the cheapest way to cut heating bills, and it makes any later heat pump work better. Here is what PPL pays and how to claim it.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Allentown
cards_intro: We re-read PPL Electric's attic, wall, rim joist, basement wall and air sealing pages on October 5, 2026. Each item was listed with its own Apply for Rebate button.

cards.title: Attic insulation
cards.note: The higher amount is for customers who qualify for PPL's enhanced offers. The new R-value must be higher than the old one.

cards.title: Exterior wall insulation
cards.note: Same two levels as attic insulation.

cards.title: Rim joist insulation
cards.note: The band where the house sits on the foundation. A common leak in basements.

cards.title: Basement wall insulation
cards.note: Needs at least R-15 continuous or R-19 cavity insulation. Basement spaces count only if they are permanent living space.

cards.title: Air sealing
cards.note: Paid at $0.25 for each CFM of air leakage you remove, with pre and post blower door tests, a 10% minimum improvement and a $25 minimum rebate.

after_cards:
Working it out

Say your air sealing cuts leakage by 400 CFM. At $0.25 per CFM that is $100, which is above the $25 minimum and below the $150 cap. Add attic insulation and the standard level pays up to $200 more. Each item is "up to", and PPL says each pays 75% of the project cost at most, so a cheap job can earn less than the headline amount.
sections: Who can claim: the heating rule

PPL pays only for rooms that are permanent living space and are conditioned by an electric heat source, or by central air conditioning where the heat is not electric. Workshops, garages, crawl spaces and outbuildings do not count, and neither does new construction. In Allentown, where 39.5% of households heat with electricity and 44.2% with gas, that matters. A gas-heated house with central A/C can qualify. A gas-heated house with no central A/C probably cannot, so check before you hire.

Allentown's homes are old. The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) shows 82.1% of homes were built before 1980, and 37.9% before 1940. Homes from that era were often built with little or no insulation in the walls and a thin layer in the attic. Many have had some work since, but plenty have not.

How you heat matters too. 39.5% of Allentown households heat with electricity and 14.1% with fuel oil. Both are costly ways to heat a leaky house. Insulation and air sealing cut the heat you need, whatever the fuel.

36.0% of Allentown homes are rowhouses or twins. Shared walls already block a lot of heat loss, so the attic, the front and back walls, and the basement rim joist do most of the leaking. That is good news: those are exactly the three insulation jobs PPL pays for.

Air sealing stops warm air from escaping through gaps. Insulation slows heat moving through solid surfaces. Doing them in that order matters, because insulation laid over open gaps lets air keep leaking through. A good contractor will seal the attic floor before adding insulation on top.

PPL's store notes that some customers qualify for larger rebates and free extra services based on income. The $500 level for insulation is one of those. Run PPL's Check Best Offers questions before you book work, since free services could cover part of the job.
Where to start in your own home

On a cold day, walk your house. Drafts at outlets on outside walls, a cold floor over the basement, and ice dams or bare spots of snow on the roof all point to heat leaking out. The attic is usually the cheapest place to start, because it is easy to reach and warm air rises straight into it. Hollow walls in many older homes can also be filled with blown-in insulation through small holes, without opening the walls.

claim_heading: How to get a PPL insulation rebate
claim_steps: Run PPL's Check Best Offers tool to see your rebate level.
Check that the space is permanent living space with electric heat, or central A/C with non-electric heat.
Get quotes that list each item separately: air sealing, attic, walls, rim joist, basement wall.
Have the work done and keep itemized invoices with the labor cost.
Apply for each item on PPL's rebate store.
faq: How much does PPL pay for insulation in Allentown?
Up to $200 for each of attic, exterior wall and rim joist insulation, or up to $500 each if you qualify for PPL's enhanced offer. Air sealing is up to $150.
Can I do the work myself?

PPL asks for a labor invoice with each insulation claim, so a do-it-yourself job does not fit. Air sealing must follow BPI standards with blower door tests before and after, which needs a trained contractor.
Do I need to heat with electricity?
Not only. The space must be conditioned by an electric heat source, or by central A/C if the heat is not electric. Gas homes without central A/C probably do not qualify.

Is there a federal insulation tax credit?
No. Federal home energy credits ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
How is the air sealing rebate worked out?
PPL pays $0.25 per CFM of air leakage removed, measured by blower door tests before and after. You need a 10% minimum improvement and a $25 minimum rebate, up to $150.
